subject.title: Cross-domain obligations and selective semantic invalidation

semantics.desiredOutcome: An accepted domain publication can create only authorized typed obligations for another domain, and authoritative semantic lineage can make exactly the affected downstream claims, obligations and work non-current when an upstream semantic subject changes without introducing cross-domain dispatch or whole-stage reset.
semantics.currentState: The delivered system now includes the A.1 organization boundary plus bounded domain execution control and mutation-current authoritative publication (A15/A16). It still does not provide domain write authority for cross-domain semantic products, semantic claim/obligation currentness heads, authoritative product derivation edges, typed cross-domain obligations, or selective dependency invalidation.

requiredBehaviors.statement: Domain write authority is explicit, immutable/versioned and separate from organizational claim authority and domain execution policy.
Authoritative semantic claims and cross-domain obligations are immutable assertions whose currentness is represented separately through durable currentness heads and transitions.
A CrossDomainObligation states the required outcome and derivation for a target domain while leaving target worker, execution policy, execution strategy, runtime and priority outside the obligation.
Target-domain materialization resolves and verifies the exact obligation, issuance authority, current input subjects and ordinary materialization authorization before creating organizational work.
Only accepted derivation edges published through an authoritative domain publication boundary enter product dependency truth; strategy-proposed lineage remains candidate evidence.
Upstream semantic currentness changes invalidate the exact reverse transitive closure of authoritative dependent subjects instead of resetting artifact containers, roles or lifecycle stages.

Publication and obligation issuance revalidate exact consumed input currentness across the publication window so a racing upstream supersession cannot leave a newly published dependent silently current.

If already-materialized or claimed work becomes semantically stale, reconciliation uses canonical organizational lifecycle invalidation and execution fencing rather than deleting work or mutating lifecycle state out of band.

The first executable cross-domain slice carries accepted BA requirement subjects into a typed SA solution-design obligation and allows accepted SA architecture subjects to issue only explicitly authorized downstream obligation kinds.

invariants.statement: Dependency edge is not work ordering.
Invalidation is not organization or workflow-stage reset.
Product semantic lineage and Blackboard work lifecycle are distinct state spaces.
Claim authority, execution policy and domain write authority do not imply one another.
Historical accepted claims and obligations remain reconstructable after becoming stale, revoked or superseded.
Container revision alone is not sufficient authority to invalidate unrelated semantic subjects.
Semantic equivalence guessed by an LLM cannot prune required invalidation in the first implementation slice.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: One accepted BA requirement subject can produce an authorized solution-design obligation that deterministically materializes SA-owned work without the BA domain selecting SA execution mechanics.
Accepted SA output can publish architecture subjects and only obligation kinds allowed by current domain write authority.
Changing one detail requirement makes only its architecture/detail dependents non-current while unrelated list claims and work remain current.
A newly published dependent racing upstream supersession cannot remain silently current after the publication currentness handshake.
Replaying the same normalized obligation publication converges on one logical immutable obligation revision; semantic change creates a superseding revision instead of mutation in place.
Stale or revoked obligations cannot materialize new target work, and already-claimed stale work loses executable capability through canonical invalidation/fencing.
Authoritative lineage/currentness state can be reconstructed from immutable claims, obligations, publication receipts, edges and transitions without relying on disposable impact caches.

outOfScope.statement: Autonomous DOMAIN_ACTIVATION, event-driven wake-up and FE/BE parallel autonomy.
Global ProductStateProjection, product-completeness or closure semantics.
Global organization scheduler, role-stage workflow or next-domain dispatcher.
Generic graph database or generic semantic-equivalence engine.
